I haven't owned a T.V. since 2001 and I have not seen any T.V. programs in my own house since, at least 2009. P.P.V. never seemed to cater to me because the sports I watch were never really popular anyway.

 

Well, since online advertising is booming now, I rather be amused by the ads when using a different IP address. Somehow British, Turkish, and Swiss ads fascinate me. German ads make want to relearn that language. It's sad that T.V. ads do not offer this.

 

The last time I watched ESPN was with my family over a college football game. That's about it. I go online for my sports, because again, they are not really popular in America. However, ESPN3 does offer some bonus material on my ISP that I occasionally stream online.

 

The best way to watch Network T.V. shows is through DVR or wait until the first season is on DVD / Blu-Ray. That way you skip the commercials and add a very valuable 15 minutes to your day! ^.^ Anything else, YouTube it!

 

I usually way reruns if it is on YouTube, Amazon Instant Video, or Netflix. If not, I can search for it by using the watch 'x' series 'season' 'episode' format (title s1e1) free online and I usually can get the desired result within a few minutes. It would be awesome though if the reruns ran with the originally commercials in them. Like a nostalgic trip through time.

 

I find it more annoying if they have cable or satellite, internet, and phone and they watch T.V. not sure if they know if the internet works or not (plus they don't want you on it) and then says "You can have the remote now." after their show is off, making me watch shit T.V. until I can leave. I'll bring my tablet with me instead, thank you very much. Internet only. Internet all the way.

Speaking to the ad's,

I watch a lot of professional Korean Starcraft 2. The advertisements they have are so bizarre to me, I genuinely enjoy them. Can't say the same for american ads. They make me feel stupid, and I get offended that these companies feel they are being successful with such ridiculous, low brow advertisements.

If Youtube fails you, another website that you will be almost guaranteed to find what you're looking for on is Dailymotion. I don't know about adverts though, I haven't unblocked ads for anyone in a long long time. Advertisers tend to abuse it as much as possible by being as intrusive and annoying as possible and even websites that I would like to support by allowing ads don't seem to even check or care how it is being abused on their site (Nexus Mods is my best example of this). I'd love to enjoy adverts like you do but usually they just cause me to want to head butt my computer screen.

As far as leaving TV behind goes, it's not always that easy, even with internet. If I spent my days streaming shows off of the internet I would be blocked by my ISP for exceeding the monthly 'fair usage limit'. And that's without ever downloading something, viva la third world.

I honestly resort to torrents (which can only be downloaded between midnight and 6am or else once again I will be blocked) and have a nice library of movies and series stored on my computer that I can watch anytime, with or without internet. Our TV is a joke, our internet is a joke and we have one satellite TV company that has the monopoly over any channel anyone would want to actually watch.

Until things change, the only things I will ever stream are WWE and the odd sport I want to take a look at from time to time. Piracy and physical hard copies are the best (and often only) solution available if I actually want to have a choice in what I see.

Perhaps I'm wrong in this assessment, but I believe Americans are fed up with being told how to spend our money on things we want, as well as the nonsensical idea that more is better.

I subscribe to Netflix because I enjoy watching television shows I've already seen again and again. That may seem strange to some of you, but it helps add a level of comfort and stability to my life (I move around a lot, and it offers a semblance of home).

The problem with purchasing bulk television channels is I don't have that option. Let's assume that I only watched Comedy Central. This station was the entire reason for my $100+ a month bill. I decide that Hey, I can find most of that content online using their website, or I can find highlight-clips of the various news channels they (had), Jon Stewart and Colbert. When I call to cancel my service, I'm borderline berated by the customer-retention representative. They offer to give me MORE channels in hopes that I'll stay. They offer to cut my bill by some marginal amount. Then they try to make me feel bad because I will have less than the girl across the street. I This is not an okay thing to have in our society. I want to pay for what I want, not what you want me to pay for.

I personally feel, with at least my generation(25~), that we are becoming less and less consumerist and more buyers of specific merchandise. The evidence for this is very circumstantial around my own life / friends, however, most people I know will gladly go out of their way to buy JUST what they need instead of searching for bulk, bargain deals. Perhaps this comes down to the economic climate we have lived with since the mid/late 2000's, or maybe its a conscious understanding with the advent of the internet that our planet is finite and excess waste is a bad thing. Either way, I feel this is a good change.

Some may argue that this selective-purchasing is a bad thing: it stifles the economy, big corporations have less income, and it hurts the middle class in the long run. I feel the opposite. I grew up in a small town with mom-and-pop shops, and we, as a community, did just fine for ourselves. Everyone could pay their bills, they could have a little money to get together at the bar and have fun, my family personally used to be able to go on vacations, and life was generally good. Then Wal-Mart came to our town and slowly ruined everything, but that's a conversation for another topic. I personally long for those days when we could get by on our own, and honestly, I feel the root of that problem has been because of corporations feeling the need to pressure us into buying more and more, instead of the consumer buying what they need and saving the rest.

Perhaps I got a bit off of the original thought, here, and for that I apologize, but it's something I feel pretty passionate about. I feel consumers should collectively and consciously search for deals that benefit them, without being wasteful of their hard earned dollars.

I only speak for myself but I'd say people want to pick what shows they want not just pick channels or packages. Why should I pay you money to send me crap shows that I have no interest in. So I don't buy any cable TV and haven't done so for over ten years.
Chin up, homie. Eventually it won't matter a bit. Good luck.
